results.title: NVIDIA H100 Price: Buying vs Renting per Hour
results.author: Faiz Ahmed
highlights:
H100 PCIe, from $2.59/GPU-hr.

The honest answer is $25,000 to $36,000 for one H100 card, and NVIDIA does not publish a list price. The low end is the street price Tom's Hardware reported for the PCIe version in August 2023, and the high end is what CNBC said some retailers had asked before April 2023, without naming the version. A distributor still listed it at $35,315.93 on 2026-09-28, and eBay listings went past $40,000 in 2023. Renting the same GPU on QuantaCloud costs $2.59/GPU-hr. At the $2.59 per GPU-hour it cost on 2026-09-27, a card at $25,000 to $35,316 equals 9,653 to 13,635 hours of rental, which is 13 to 19 months of round-the-clock use (our calculation, below). The SXM H100 has no card price I can quote: it ships on 4- and 8-GPU HGX boards inside complete servers.

...

## What renting an H100 costs on QuantaCloud#

An H100 PCIe rents for $2.59/GPU-hr on QuantaCloud, billed by the hour. These are the live configurations:

| GPUs | vCPU | RAM | Disk | Region | Per hour | Per GPU-hour | Launch |

Prices checked 14 Nov 2026, 13:25 UTC

The hourly price covers a whole VM, not only the GPU. On 2026-09-27 the single-GPU H100 VM came with 20 vCPU, 128 GB of RAM and 1,250 GB of disk in us-midwest-2, running Ubuntu 22.04 with the NVIDIA driver and Docker. Billing runs from a prepaid balance with a $5 minimum deposit. The first hour is charged at launch, each further hour is charged when the previous one is used up, and the unused seconds of the current hour are refunded when you stop. There are no egress or ingress charges. Stopping terminates the VM and deletes its disk, so copy your results off first. The pricing page and the billing docs have the full rules, and the H100 page covers the specs and what fits in 80 GB. The GPU cost calculator applies those rules to your own hours at the live price. SXM H100 servers are not on demand: they are the reserved builds described above.

results.title: What Is GPU as a Service (GPUaaS)? Models and Pricing
results.author: Faiz Ahmed
highlights:
## How GPUaaS pricing works#

The unit is the GPU-hour: an hourly price for each GPU, times the number of GPUs, times the hours. Two offers at the same GPU-hour price can still cost very different amounts, because of what sits around that price.

| What to check | Why it changes the bill | On QuantaCloud |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Billing granularity and minimums | A 10-minute test billed as a full hour pays for 6 times the time it used (our calculation: 60 / 10) | The first hour is charged at launch, and the unused seconds are refunded when you stop |
| What the hourly price includes | CPU, RAM and disk can be billed separately | vCPU, RAM and a local disk come with each configuration, for example 16 vCPU, 180 GB of RAM and 750 GB of disk with one H200 NVL on 2026-09-27 |
| Data transfer | Moving datasets and checkpoints out can be charged per GB | No egress or ingress charges |
| Storage after you stop | Volumes that outlive an instance are billed per GB per month | No volumes or snapshots: stopping deletes the disk |
| Payment | Prepaid credit or a monthly invoice | Prepaid credit by card, from $5, with optional auto top-up |
| Commitment | A term buys capacity held for you | None on demand. Reserved terms are quoted in writing |

QuantaCloud 的计费方式有点特别。

它不是“每秒从余额里一点点扣”，而是：

启动时先扣一小时，停止时再把这一小时里没用掉的秒数退回来。

Read this before you compare the two tables. A TPU chip and a GPU are not equivalent units. They differ in memory per chip, in how many chips come attached to one host, and in what software runs on them. A lower price per chip-hour does not mean a lower cost per trained model or per generated token. Google's prices above are list prices from one vendor. The GPU prices are the cheapest live listing across many vendors. We have not benchmarked TPUs against GPUs, and this page gives no performance ratio because we do not have one we trust.

results.title: H100 price per hour, October 2026: 11 clouds compared · ClearCompute
results.author: Ronit Ahuja
highlights:
The short answer

On 5 October 2026, one H100 80GB SXM listed at $2.69 to $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand across nine clouds, and the Vast.ai marketplace median was $1.80. Five specialist clouds charged between $3.20 and $4.50. The hyperscalers charged $6.88 (AWS), $11.06 (Google Cloud) and $12.29 (Azure), though a three-year commitment brings them down to between $2.97 and $5.40. For an inference server, four things matter as much as the rate: the smallest unit you can rent, egress, billing increments and how fast the price is moving.

...

## SXM, PCIe and NVL are different products#

"H100" covers three cards with different memory and bandwidth:

| H100 variant | Memory | Memory bandwidth | Lowest on-demand price we found |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SXM | 80 GB | 3.35 TB/s | $2.69 (RunPod Community) |
| PCIe | 80 GB | 2.0 TB/s | $1.99 (RunPod Community) |
| NVL | 94 GB | 3.9 TB/s | $2.59 (RunPod Community) |

Each generated token requires reading the model's weights from memory, so for a single stream of text the speed limit is memory bandwidth rather than compute. NVIDIA's inference guide walks through why. Per unit of bandwidth, the SXM card is the better buy: $2.69 for 3.35 TB/s works out at $0.80 per TB/s-hour, against $1.00 for the PCIe card at $1.99.

...

## Prices rose this autumn#

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on 1 October: H100 by 17% ($3.85 to $4.50), H200 by 20% and B200 by 19%.
- AWS announced a 15% rise in EC2 Capacity Block prices from 7 October, taking a P5 H100 from $5.19 to $5.97 per GPU-hour.
- Verda's H100 went from $3.37 on 22 September to $3.77 on 5 October, up 12% in 13 days, according to the Wayback Machine's captures of its price page.

Any price survey goes stale within weeks, this one included. For today's number, live trackers such as gpufinder.dev, which polls 22 vendors every hour, and SkyPilot's GPU Compass are better sources. A survey is more useful for explaining what the number buys.

results.title: GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.
highlights:
# GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers. · 2026-09-22T00:00:00+00:00

GPU pricing is increasing across the board, but the severity of those increases varies greatly across providers.

Take H100 pricing as an example.

In 2026, providers in our network have raised their H100 rates by an average of 31.6%.

However, between these providers, their individual H100 pricing has increased as much as 47.5%, and as little as 13.6%.

Movement in GPU pricing as a whole only tells part of the story.

There is still significant price variance between operators, even those with near identical architectures.
